commonsFile: File:2023-11-04 A view from Lycian Way near Kaş 1.jpg
location: Lycian Way near Kaş, Antalya Province
alt: View over the Lycian coast and the Mediterranean from the waymarked Lycian Way near Kaş
caption: The Lycian Way above Kaş: a footpath over limestone headlands with the Mediterranean and the Greek island of Meis in view. The coast section from Fethiye to Antalya is the spine of this trip, walked in day sections with a base each night.

commonsFile: File:Patara - the beach from the sand dunes - panoramio.jpg
alt: Long empty sandy beach seen from the dunes at Patara
caption: Patara's 18 km beach and dunes behind the ruins of the Lycian capital. In March it is empty, and the site doubles as a protected nesting beach, so it is a walk rather than a swim stop.

location: Kekova Sound near Üçağız and Simena, Antalya Province
alt: Submerged Lycian ruins seen through clear water in the Kekova Sound
caption: Walls and stairways of a Lycian settlement drowned by earthquakes and now lying just below the surface at Kekova. A small local boat or sea kayak from Üçağız drifts over them; no diving is permitted on the protected site.

alt: Lycian rock-cut tombs with carved temple fronts in a cliff face at Myra
caption: Cliff-face tombs at Myra carved to imitate timber houses with pediments and columns. They show the Lycian habit of burying the dead high up in the rock, and they are quiet in March.

commonsFile: File:Northern Yanartaş flame close to Pass Chimaera.jpg
alt: Natural gas flames burning from cracks in rock on a hillside at the Chimaera
caption: The Chimaera, where methane seeping through the rock has burned for millennia on the slope above Çıralı. Visited after dark on foot with head torches, it is the one night-time walk of the trip and a good reason to camp or lodge in Çıralı.

location: Termessos, Güllük Dağı National Park, Antalya Province
alt: Ruins of the ancient mountain city of Termessos among pines on a steep slope
caption: Termessos, a Pisidian city built on a steep mountain shelf that Alexander the Great did not take. It stands inside a national park at about 1,000 m, where March is cool and the site has almost no visitors.

alt: Panorama of the ruins of Sagalassos below the Taurus mountains
caption: Sagalassos, a Hellenistic and Roman city at about 1,500 m in the Taurus, under long-running excavation by a Belgian-led team. Snow is possible here into March, which is the reason the visit sits late in the route.

commonsFile: File:Panoramic view of Eğirdir and Lake Eğirdir from Akpınar, March 2024 08.jpg
location: Eğirdir and Lake Eğirdir, Isparta Province
alt: Panoramic view of Eğirdir town on its peninsula and the lake in March
caption: Eğirdir on its peninsula in the Lake District, photographed in March. The town is a lakeside rest stop between the coast and the Taurus, with snow often still on the surrounding peaks.

alt: Mount Babadağ rising above the coast and bay at Ölüdeniz
caption: Babadağ rises to about 1,970 m directly above Ölüdeniz and the first Lycian Way stages. Tandem paragliding from the summit is offered by licensed operators and is the optional adrenaline day of the first part of the trip.

location: Lycian Way, Muğla or Antalya Province
alt: Cairns marking a stony section of the Lycian Way
caption: Cairns and red-and-white paint stripes mark the Lycian Way over rocky ground. The route is waymarked, but in March some higher sections are muddy or snowed in, so each day is chosen locally.

alt: Temple foundations and columns at the Letoon sanctuary beside reeds and water
caption: Letoon, the federal sanctuary of the Lycians and part of the Xanthos-Letoon World Heritage property. The temples of Leto, Artemis and Apollo stand in a flooded, frog-filled meadow in late winter.

alt: Steep rock walls of Saklıkent Gorge
caption: Saklıkent, a gorge about 18 km long cut into the Akdağ massif. In March the meltwater is cold and strong, so the walkway section is done on the footbridges and only the lower reach on foot.
